about.text: Casein, milk's main protein, precipitated out of skimmed milk by acid at its isoelectric point, pH 4.6 to 4.7, then washed and dried. Used in foods and industry, dissolved in alkali to make caseinates, and once the base of casein glues.

how.text: Casein carries a negative charge in milk (pH 6.6). At pH 4.6 the charge is gone, the micelles collapse and clump into curd, which is washed free of lactose and minerals, then dried and ground. Lactic acid from a starter can do the same job, but industrial acid casein is mostly made with mineral acid.

steps.note: With 10 % hydrochloric acid to pH 4.6, the isoelectric point of casein.
The curd is cooled to about 20 °C.

steps.name: wash
steps.note: With up to 1 l of water per l of milk.
In a fluid bed, from about 45 % to about 90 % dry matter.
